clue.text: Wash here, but returned to the city

parts.note: Bath is a Roman spa city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone told to go and wash somewhere, but heading back to town instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The city comes first in the answer although it is last in the clue; BATH TUB joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathtub is the vessel in which one bathes, so it is literally a place where you wash.

clue.text: Confronted someone hirsute

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to beard someone is to face them boldly, past tense
second meaning: having a beard, hairy-faced

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to a hairy person.
explanation.walkthrough: To beard a lion in its den is to confront it; the same word as an adjective means having a beard.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the verb beard means faced boldly, and the adjective describes a man wearing facial hair, which is hairy.

clue.text: Characteristic pity misplaced by state

indicators.note: letters that are misplaced have been put in the wrong order and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A sad sign of the times: compassion lost because of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Something characteristic is typical of its kind, showing its usual qualities.

clue.text: So Underhill found a trunk

parts.note: read as under plus hill: a tor is a rocky hill, and the piece before goes beneath it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mr Underhill, Frodo's alias in The Lord of the Rings, comes across a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Underhill reads as one name, but must be split into two words; in a down entry, the piece under another follows it in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the main body of a person apart from head and limbs, which is the torso.

clue.text: 007's female slave?

parts.note: 007 is the code number of James Bond
a female person

explanation.surface: A question about James Bond's girlfriend being in thrall to him.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bond woman (a Bond girl) becomes a word for a female serf; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A bondwoman is a woman held in bondage, a female serf or slave.

clue.text: Categorised journalist on form

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece sitting on another comes after it

parts.note: a form is a school class
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is pigeonholed by how they are performing.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To class things is to sort them into groups, so classed means categorised.

clue.text: Turn trick on its head somewhere in Africa

indicators.note: in a down answer the head is the top, so the second piece is placed above the first

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: An instruction to invert a magic trick, located somewhere on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On its head' suggests turning upside down, but it only places the trick at the top of the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Congo is a country and river in central Africa, so it is a place on that continent.

clue.text: Newly clean, yet egghead produces gas

indicators.note: newly suggests made afresh, so the letters are formed into something new

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
read as the head of egg, its first letter

explanation.surface: A freshly washed intellectual still gives off fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like a brainy person but means the top letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetylene is a flammable hydrocarbon gas used in welding torches.

clue.text: Therefore legal to beg?

parts.note: so means therefore
licit means lawful, the opposite of illicit

explanation.surface: A question whether begging is therefore within the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask earnestly for something, which is to beg or plead.

clue.text: Detective inspector strangely sad in showing contempt

parts.note: DI is the police abbreviation for detective inspector

indicators.note: strangely means oddly or out of the ordinary, so the letters are set out differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer, oddly downcast, shows scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is the feeling that someone is unworthy of respect, the same as contempt.

clue.text: Some aspiring candidates get medication

indicators.note: some means only a part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the first word

explanation.surface: Hopeful job applicants are prescribed a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the word aspiring minus its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling drug, a standard medication.

clue.text: It's not necessary for sewing equipment to be pointless

indicators.note: a compass point such as south is an abbreviation; pointless means one is removed

parts.note: something not necessary is needless

explanation.surface: A claim that sewing kit has no need of sharp tips.
explanation.walkthrough: S, for south, is the compass point dropped from the end. 'Pointless' sits naturally with needles, but it is the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles are the sharp tools used to stitch thread through fabric when sewing.

clue.text: "Torchwood" perverted science fiction here

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that the TV series Torchwood has corrupted its parent show's genre.
explanation.walkthrough: Torchwood is itself a spin-off of the answer, a long-running BBC science-fiction television series.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Who is a BBC television drama in the science-fiction genre, so science fiction is found there.

clue.text: Expression of disgust at being given a plant

parts.words: Expression of disgust at being given a
parts.note: yuck is a cry of disgust, and here it is given an a

explanation.surface: Someone says ugh on being handed a pot plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, yuck and a make the name of the plant; there is no separate signal for the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The yucca is a spiky-leaved plant of the agave family, often kept as a houseplant.

clue.text: Sold 50 poor toys

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters are knocked into another order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A shop's sales report: fifty shoddy playthings sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolls are figures of people that children play with, a classic kind of toy.

clue.text: My darling pudding head!

parts.note: in Britain a sweet is a dessert or pudding
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: An affectionate cry to a beloved, silly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pudding head' reads as a fond insult, but each word supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetness is used as a term of endearment for a loved one, as is my darling.

clue.text: Ragged flier taken in

parts.note: a moth is a flying insect
food taken in has been eaten

explanation.surface: A scruffy pilot has been fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests deceived, but here it means consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten clothes have been chewed by moth larvae, so they are shabby and ragged.

clue.text: Board embracing different role is fairly good

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are put in another order
to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a board is a table, as in bed and board
the word role rearranged

explanation.surface: A company board takes on a changed role and does reasonably well.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerable means acceptable or passable, so moderately good rather than excellent.

clue.text: Baroness Orczy's blooming hero

parts.note: surface reading: the bloody hero of Orczy's novels, with blooming as a mild British oath
setter's reading: the hero is named after a flowering plant, so blooming is literal

explanation.walkthrough: Baroness Orczy wrote The Scarlet Pimpernel, whose hero takes his name from a small red wild flower; 'blooming' is British slang for 'damned' as well as 'in flower'.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is both a flowering plant and the alias of Orczy's swashbuckling hero.

clue.text: Participate in average amount received

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
the take is the money received, as in a day's takings

explanation.surface: Taking part in sharing out a typical haul.
explanation.definitionFit: To partake is to take part in something, which is to participate.

clue.text: Noble Mother Earth, originally without an insect

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the pieces go around something

parts.note: ma is an informal name for a mother
a gnat is a small biting fly

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Earth

explanation.surface: Gaia, the Mother Earth goddess, in her first form had no bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother Earth' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces; 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnate was originally a great noble, and is now a powerful wealthy person; noble here is a noun.

clue.text: Bird spotted in the Beagle Channel

indicators.note: something spotted in a place is seen sitting inside it

parts.note: the letters after the first in the first word

explanation.surface: A sighting of a bird in a strait at the tip of South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beagle Channel, named after Darwin's ship, is a strait at Tierra del Fuego.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Weapon fired at whale reported from top of ship's side

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is judged by its sound

parts.note: a wale is a ridge or plank, and sounds the same as the sea creature

explanation.surface: A harpoon gun is aimed at a whale from the side of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is usually said 'gunnel', but the sea mammal is heard in its spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of a boat's side, once where guns were mounted.

clue.text: The Spanish agent becomes stylish

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: becomes says the word changes into something else, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy from Spain turns into a smart dresser.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, much the same as stylish.

clue.text: Nothing left? Correct

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the opposite side to left, so not left at all

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing left?' reads as asking whether anything remains, but it means the direction that is no part of left.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the side opposite left and also means true or accurate.

clue.text: Arrange small company differently, with exaggerated pride

indicators.note: differently means done another way, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Co is the short form of company

explanation.surface: Advice to restructure a little firm, done with conceit.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is an overbearing sense of one's own importance, an excess of pride.

clue.text: One point almost providing protective cover

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
a prong is a sharp point, as on a fork

explanation.surface: A single sharp tip nearly gives shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a garment tied over the front to protect clothes, so a protective covering.

clue.text: Taking time out; ignite new spirits

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the remaining letters are given a fresh order
time is abbreviated to a single letter, and taking it out removes it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pausing to light fresh drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: T stands for time; 'spirits' looks like alcohol, but means supernatural beings.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genie or genius, guardian spirits or jinn of Arabian tales.

clue.text: It's unprofessional to place close friend in an old city

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the others

parts.note: taken as the single letter
a mate is a pal or close friend
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, the crossword's usual old city

explanation.surface: A warning that housing your best mate in an ancient town is unbusinesslike.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur as an adjective means done without professional skill or payment, hence unprofessional.

clue.text: Scarf ring — primarily a nineties' accessory

parts.note: a band is a ring, as a wedding band

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A neckerchief and a ring were the fashion add-ons of the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandana is a large patterned square of cloth worn as a scarf or headscarf.

clue.text: Unusually, mere boy becomes a poet

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: Remarkably, a mere lad turns into a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American essayist and poet of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Obvious that net was damaged by clumsy dive

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so these letters are reassembled
a clumsy move is awkward and disordered, so these letters are rearranged too

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is plain that the goal net was broken by a goalkeeper's awkward dive.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plain to see, clearly apparent, the same as obvious.
